clue.text: Not at all-and I mean, all !

definitions.text: Not at all-and I mean, all !

parts.words: Not at all-and I mean, all !
parts.note: an emphatic denial, the speaker stressing that not even the smallest part is true

explanation.surface: Someone flatly denies a suggestion, stressing that they mean every word.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is an emphatic denial; the colloquial phrase that means the same is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a hearty British way of saying absolutely not, refusing even the smallest share of a claim.

clue.text: Train brothers to chant; it can make people feel better

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Train brothers to chant; it can make people feel better' (7) for NURSING: SING is 'chant', but no reading of 'Train brothers' gives NUR, so a word looks misprinted and no source was found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Train brothers to chant; it can make people feel better

clue.text: Diets adapted for seasons

indicators.note: adapted means changed to suit, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dieter changes their menus to suit the time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges DIETS. 'Seasons' is the old sense of tide kept in Yuletide and Eastertide.
explanation.definitionFit: Tide is an old word for a time of year, surviving in Christmastide and Whitsuntide.

clue.text: Innocent lamb mutilated-pointless

indicators.note: mutilated means badly damaged, so the letters of the animal are mangled into a new order

parts.note: split as point-less: a point of the compass is E, and -less gives LESS

explanation.surface: A gruesome report of a lamb pointlessly maimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutilated' rearranges LAMB into BLAM. 'pointless' is read in two parts: E (east, a compass point) followed by LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without fault deserves no censure, so they are free of any reproach or guilt.

clue.text: Ends of cues

definitions.meaning: the pointed extremities of things, as of a finger or a snooker cue
hints or helpful suggestions, as a racing punter gets

explanation.surface: The leather ends of snooker cues.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: extremities at the point of a thing, and helpful hints or pointers given to someone.

clue.text: Rounded up the figure?

parts.note: read not as arithmetic but as making someone's body rounder by feeding them up

explanation.surface: An accountant rounds a number up to the next whole one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounded up' and 'figure' suggest arithmetic; the figure is a body, made rounder.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeding someone up makes their body plumper, so their figure has been rounded out.

clue.text: Roots out somebody's trunk

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the word before are shuffled

explanation.surface: A gardener digs out the roots of a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ROOTS. 'Trunk' is a person's body, not a tree's.
explanation.definitionFit: The human body without head and limbs is called the trunk.

clue.text: Soggy grounding around, awfully dull look out for Oxbridge

indicators.note: around means the marshy word encloses what follows

parts.note: a bog is wet, spongy ground

indicators.note: awfully means badly done, so the letters of the dull word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreary, waterlogged playing field for a university match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges DULL into ULLD, and 'around' puts BOG round it. At Oxford and Cambridge, a bulldog is a proctor's attendant who patrols for misbehaving students.
explanation.definitionFit: At the old universities the proctors' officers who keep an eye out for student misconduct are nicknamed after a dog breed.

clue.text: Tell the prince your name, flower!

definitions.text: Tell the prince your name, flower!

parts.words: Tell the prince your name, flower!
parts.note: read as a girl, told to stand when a prince calls, who is named after a spring flower

explanation.surface: A girl at court is urged to introduce herself to a visiting prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' looks like a term of endearment to the girl; it is the definition, a pale yellow spring bloom also used as a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale yellow woodland flower of early spring, also given as a girl's name.

clue.text: Rolled up when the VIPs had gone?

definitions.text: Rolled up when the VIPs had gone?

parts.words: Rolled up when the VIPs had gone?
parts.note: pictures the strip of carpet laid for dignitaries being put away after their visit

explanation.surface: The stewards tidy away after distinguished guests depart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolled up' could mean arrived; here it is what is done to a carpet once the dignitaries have left.
explanation.definitionFit: A crimson strip laid for important visitors to walk on, gathered up again afterwards.

clue.text: White-collar urbanity holds back from the country

indicators.note: back means those contained letters are read from right to left
holds means the phrase contains the letters within it

explanation.surface: Office workers' city polish is kept away from the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds back' points to LARUR inside 'white-colLAR URbanity', read backwards. 'Urbanity' tempts towards a city meaning; the answer is its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from the countryside, rather than the town, is pastoral or agricultural in character.

clue.text: Springs from the publishing house?

definitions.meaning: emerges or flows out, as water from a source
what a publisher brings out, its editions of a magazine

explanation.surface: Fresh ideas flow out of a publishing firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge or flow out is to come forth; a magazine's numbered editions are what it brings out.

clue.text: Much improved by recreation

definitions.meaning: made better, as a character after mending their ways

explanation.surface: Someone's health is much better after a holiday of leisure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recreation' is read as re-creation, making again, not leisure.
explanation.definitionFit: A changed character is a better one; to make something again is to form it anew.

clue.text: A little contrivance deftly tagged

indicators.note: deftly means nimbly handled, so the letters of the next word are skilfully rearranged

explanation.surface: A small device is neatly labelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deftly' rearranges TAGGED.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ingenious device or appliance is a handy mechanical contrivance.

clue.text: A writer's address to a group of businessmen

definitions.text: A writer's address to a group of businessmen

parts.words: A writer's address to a group of businessmen
parts.note: address means the greeting opening a formal letter to a firm, not a speech or location

explanation.surface: An author gives a talk to a meeting of executives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' suggests a speech or a location; it is the salutation that opens a business letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional salutation opening a formal letter to a company or its directors.

clue.text: Make some progress without falling out

definitions.meaning: manage or advance, as in how one is faring
be on friendly terms with no quarrels

explanation.surface: Two colleagues advance on a project without quarrelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both advancing or managing and living harmoniously with others.

clue.text: A nifty soul able to think quickly

definitions.text: A nifty soul able to think quickly

parts.words: A nifty soul able to think quickly
parts.note: soul is read as the intellect, a nimble one that reasons fast

explanation.surface: A description of a quick-witted, sprightly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soul' looks like a person; it is the mental faculty, quick and nimble.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimble intellect is one that reasons fast and adapts readily.

clue.text: The players won't get away with such triumphs

definitions.text: The players won't get away with such triumphs

parts.words: The players won't get away with such triumphs
parts.note: get away is read as playing at an away ground, so these victories are on the team's own pitch

explanation.surface: A warning that cheats among the team will be caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't get away with' suggests escaping punishment; it means the team is not playing away from its own ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Victories achieved on a team's own ground, in front of its supporters, rather than on an opponent's.

clue.text: Burning blotchy skin results from kitchen chore

definitions.meaning: a red, itchy patch on the skin caused by warmth
read as warms a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: A cook ends up with a rash after a stint at the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the phrase differently: someone who heats (a) pot is doing a kitchen chore.
explanation.definitionFit: A red skin blemish brought on by warmth; split differently, the words describe warming a cooking vessel.

clue.text: … but have high expectations, apparently

parts.note: follows on from the clue before, describing a team or person full of optimism

explanation.surface: Players or supporters cherish lofty ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 17 Down, as if the team at home expects to win; 'apparently' signals that the word reads as full of hope.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone expecting much is optimistic, brimming with expectation of success.

clue.text: Make a heap from a multiple crash

definitions.meaning: stack things into a mound, accumulate
a road accident involving many vehicles

explanation.surface: A crash on the motorway leaves a heap of wrecked cars.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to stack or accumulate; as a noun, a road collision involving many vehicles.

clue.text: Go before President and then go back again

parts.note: to recede is to withdraw or move back

explanation.surface: A head of state leads a procession, then retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and then' is a link joining P and the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To come or happen earlier than something else is to lead or antecede it.

clue.text: Easy work with a bulldozer

parts.note: read literally as something a bulldozer could shove over, and figuratively as an easy task

explanation.surface: Demolition is no trouble with heavy machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: The figurative sense, an easy task or a soft touch, is pictured as something a bulldozer topples.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy task, or a person easily overcome, is a walkover or soft touch.

clue.text: The play scored

parts.note: scored is read as set to music, so the drama is a sung one

explanation.surface: A theatre production was a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' looks like success; it means written in musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama set to music and sung throughout, as staged at Covent Garden.

clue.text: Persons prepared to quietly elope

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or set up, so the letters of the word for running off are rearranged

explanation.surface: A couple are ready to run off together without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges ELOPE into EOPLE, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Human beings considered collectively; the plural of person in everyday use.

clue.text: This, sahib, is the gentleman

parts.note: points to the Anglo-Indian phrase for a true gentleman, completed by the word sahib

explanation.surface: A servant in India introduces a visitor to his master.
explanation.walkthrough: In Anglo-Indian English a pukka sahib was a genuine gentleman; the answer is the word that goes before 'sahib'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi for ripe or solid, used by the British Raj to mean genuine or proper.

clue.text: Giles's place is over mile distant

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: far means a long way off

explanation.surface: Someone's home lies more than a mile away.
explanation.walkthrough: Farmer Giles is a stock name for a British farmer, so his place is where he works.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmer Giles is the stock comic figure of an English countryman, and his holding is agricultural land.

clue.text: Stuffing a hollow formality

definitions.meaning: forcemeat for filling poultry, from French farcir, to stuff
a ridiculous sham or empty pretence

explanation.surface: Cooking the stuffing has become an empty ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: The old culinary sense is forcemeat; a sham proceeding is also called a mockery or travesty.

clue.text: Where to seek preservation from such a plight?

definitions.text: Where to seek preservation from such a plight?

parts.words: Where to seek preservation from such a plight?
parts.note: preservation is read as the vinegar that keeps vegetables, and the place is in trouble

explanation.surface: Someone in trouble asks where to look for rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preservation' suggests rescue; it is the preserving of food in vinegar, the idiom for being in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being in difficulty or a mess, like vegetables steeped in vinegar.

clue.text: Harassed Madame "N uses a pseudonym

indicators.note: harassed means hassled and disturbed, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A flustered Frenchwoman resorts to an alias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harassed' rearranges MADAME N USES. The stray quotation mark is print noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A false name adopted to conceal identity is an alias or nom de plume.
